feedback: If a partial product is dropped (e.g. answering 320 for 45×8, forgetting 5×8), prompt: say each partial product aloud and add them; jot the parts down if working memory overloads.
If compensation is left unadjusted (99×6 = 600), ask: what did you change about 99, and what must you do to put that back? (Subtract 6 to reach 594.)

If the written column method is attempted mentally and a carry is lost (answer off by tens), suggest partitioning or doubling (45×8 = 45×4×2 = 180×2 = 360) as a carrying-free mental route; reserve columns for paper.
If order of operations is ignored in a mixed string (e.g. computing 250×(3+500)), clarify: multiply before add here — do 250×3 first, then add 500.
If the strategy is sound but a sub-total is miscomputed, do not reteach the strategy: have the learner re-state and recompute the slipped part, then check by estimation.
activities.intendedInsight: Mental calculation is about decomposing numbers flexibly using place value and the distributive/associative laws, leveraging known facts to reduce memory load, and choosing the route that suits the particular numbers — not visualising a column method.
learnerActions: Given 45 × 8, partition 45 into 40 and 5, multiply each part by 8 (40×8 = 320, 5×8 = 40), then recombine the partial products to reach 360.
Use compensation on 99 × 6: compute 100 × 6 = 600, then subtract the adjustment 6 to get 594 — stating both the rounding move and the adjust-back step.
Grow a derived-fact chain from a known core fact: from 6 × 4 reach 60 × 4, 6.5 × 4 and 12 × 4, saying how each relative is obtained.
Solve a mixed-operation string such as 250 × 3 + 500: multiply first (250 × 3 = 750), then add 500 to get 1250, stating the order used.
For at least one calculation, try two different strategies (e.g. partitioning vs doubling 45 three times) and judge which was more efficient for those numbers.
Before finalising, give a rough estimate (45 × 8 lies between 40 × 8 = 320 and 50 × 8 = 400, so around 360) and check the answer fits.
activities.title: Mental maths strategy workspace: split, compensate, derive

feedback: Reward reasoning about WHY a route is efficient for these numbers, not just fast answers.
If the learner believes there is one 'right' mental method, present a case where a different strategy is clearly quicker (e.g. 99×6 by compensation vs partitioning) to prompt flexible selection.
When comparing, ask the learner to state the condition that makes each strategy efficient (numbers near a round number favour compensation; even factors favour doubling/halving).
activities.intendedInsight: Articulating and comparing methods makes efficiency and mathematical structure explicit and shareable, and builds the metacognition behind flexible choice — the real target beyond speed.
learnerActions: After solving a calculation mentally, explain aloud how it was worked out ('I did 40×8 then 5×8 and added them').
Compare your method with a different method for the same calculation (e.g. 'you doubled 45 three times') and decide which is more efficient and why.
Respond to prompts such as: 'How did you break up 45 × 8 to make it easier?', 'Could doubling help instead?', and 'In 250 × 3 + 500, which do you do first and why?'
Judge whether a proposed shortcut is valid and efficient for the given numbers, not just whether it reaches an answer.
activities.title: Explain and compare: strategy talk

feedback: For a missing-partial item, if the blank is filled wrongly, return to the partition and recompute each part separately.
For strategy-matching, if an inefficient strategy is chosen, ask the learner to try both and time or count the steps to feel the difference.
Recognition-only matching confirms identification but does not by itself build the decomposition move; follow with an active calculation the learner performs from scratch.
activities.intendedInsight: A reference of worked strategies plus targeted practice consolidates fluency and strategy-identification, provided the learner is actively producing or completing calculations rather than only recognising answers.
learnerActions: Consult a worked reference showing partition, compensate and derive each worked once, with a note of when each is most useful, then apply the matching strategy to new calculations.
Complete fill-in-the-missing-partial items (e.g. 40×8 + __ = 360) to confirm all parts are tracked.
Match each calculation to its most efficient strategy and justify the match.
Practise derived-fact chains for fluency, timing optional, always stating the known fact the answer was derived from.
activities.title: Strategy reference and fluency practice
